nodes.notes:
• Classification: mixed dense stencil/contraction pipeline—three stride-2 padded 3x3 convolutions with GELU, followed by a dense projection and elementwise scale/position add. All accesses are regular; reductions are over input channel and 3x3 kernel dimensions, then over flattened C×F.
• Canonical math: Ti=ceil(Ti-1/2), Fi=Fi-1/2 with F:80→40→20→10. Each convolution output is GELU(bias + Σci,kh,kw input[n,ci,2f+kh-1,2t+kw-1]·weight[co,ci,kh,kw]) with zero padding. The projection is y[n,t,d]=embed_scale·Σc,f x3[n,c,f,t]·W[d,10c+f]+PE[t,d]. Outputs and independent spatial tiles can run in parallel; reductions should use FP32 accumulation.
• Layout/access: inputs and convolution weights are contiguous NCHW/OIHW BF16; PE[1500,1024] and Wout[1024,3840] are contiguous. The reference flatten order is K=10c+f. Conv1 output is approximately 30,720·B·T bytes, Conv2 3,840·B·T bytes, and Conv3 960·B·T bytes in BF16, making the first boundary the largest traffic target. Conv weights and projection weights have substantial reuse and collectively fit comfortably in A800 L2, subject to contention.
• Regimes: (1) tiny B and short T: launch latency, cold weight reads, and underfilled tiles dominate; (2) moderate B/T: layout and intermediate traffic compete with contraction compute, especially at the Conv1→Conv2 boundary; (3) long T or larger B: Conv2/3 become compute-bound and tensor-core utilization is decisive; (4) near the 1500-position output limit: total work is very large and activation footprint/allocator pressure become relevant.
• Knobs: output-channel/spatial tiling, reduction blocking, number of warps/stages, direct versus packed convolution lowering, intermediate layout, fusion of bias/GELU and terminal scale/PE, FP32 accumulation, boundary masks, and specialized short-shape dispatch.
• Skeleton: compute convolution tiles with input/weight fragments staged and FP32 accumulators in registers, apply bias/GELU before BF16 storage, repeat through three stages, then consume Conv3 directly in flatten order for projection and fuse scale plus PE into the projection epilogue. Separate kernels need no synchronization beyond launch ordering; within a tile, only staging synchronization is needed.
• Pruned families: a general materialized pipeline offers lowest correctness risk; a long-sequence traffic-minimizing plan recomputes/fuses the cheap first stage locally to avoid its large tensor; a short-workload plan prioritizes fewer launches and compact tiles. Full fusion of all three convolutions is pruned because cross-channel dependencies and halo duplication create excessive state and recomputation.

kernel_summary: This is a mixed dense-convolution and matrix-projection pipeline with regular indexing: three padded stride-2 3x3 BF16 convolutions reduce frequency 80→40→20→10 and time to ceil(time_dim/8), then a C×F=3840 reduction projects to 1024 and adds scaled positional embeddings. Conv2 and Conv3 are compute-heavy tensor-core candidates, while the very large Conv1 activation is the main bandwidth concern; tiny shapes instead risk launch latency, cold weight traffic, and poor occupancy. Correctness hinges on ceil-divided dimensions, zero-padding masks, exact flatten order K=10c+f, FP32 reduction accumulation, GELU semantics, BF16 output conversion, and ensuring the output sequence does not exceed the 1500-row positional cache.
open_questions: What exact batch_size and time_dim cases are used for scoring, and how are they weighted between short and long regimes?
Is time_after_conv always defined as ceil(time_dim/8), including odd time dimensions, or can benchmark metadata provide a different value?
Is ceil(time_dim/8) guaranteed to be at most max_source_positions=1500, or must the implementation handle or reject longer sequences?
Must GELU match PyTorch's default exact erf formulation, or is a tanh/polynomial approximation acceptable under the stated tolerance?
Does the evaluator compare against one fixed cuDNN algorithm, and are output differences from FP32 accumulation order consistently within max_atol=1.1 and max_rtol=0.05?
Are input tensors and weights guaranteed contiguous with the reference strides, or must arbitrary compatible strides be supported?
Does benchmark timing include output allocation and multiple Triton launches, and are CUDA graph or warm-cache effects present?
